newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester retreats on 2nd day.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester retreats on 2nd day.

text.p: Shares in banking group Alliance & Leicester Plc retreated in active trade on Tuesday, amid cautious press and analyst comment following the stock's rampaging market debut on Monday, dealers said.

Analysts at NatWest Securities said there was "better value elsewhere" in the sector, dealers said, and other brokerages were also cautious on the stock, which was down 30p at 536-1/2 by 1014 GMT in volume of 59.5 million shares.

"There was initial scepticism about the company, the quality of its management and its relatively small size, which gave way to talk of a stock squeeze and the need for institutions to buy into the stock," said an analyst at one leading brokerage, who asked not to be named.
"Now the situation seems to be coming back towards reality."
The analyst noted that most institutions that had bought stock at the second auction, whose results were announced earlier on Tuesday, were showing a loss on their investment.
He said he expected the weight of post-flotation selling would push the stock down to around 500p, at which point it could be time to start building up holdings.
A&L said the average price bid for its shares was 551p in the second of three planned auctions, designed to clear blocks of windfall shares owned by former A&L members.
At Goldman Sachs, analysts started coverage of the stock with a "market performer" rating.

Comment in the Financial Times Lex column set the tone for the stock, arguing that the "odds favour an early correction" in A&L's share price, and that this was made even more likely by the "high number of carpet-baggers" that the flotation had attracted.
